title: Free sugars limit
text: Keep free sugars under 10% of your daily energy, which is about 50 g on a 2,000 kcal diet. Staying under 5% may bring further benefit. Free sugars include sugars added to food or drink, as well as the sugars in honey, syrups and fruit juice.

title: How much fat
text: Total fat should be no more than 30% of daily energy, and about 15% is the usual minimum. Saturated fat should stay at or below 10% of energy. Trans fat should stay at or below 1%, and industrially produced trans fat is best avoided.
licence: Paraphrased for education. Copyright World Health Organization; see who.int terms of use.

title: Fruit and vegetables each day
text: Anyone older than 10 should aim for at least 400 g of fruit and vegetables a day.
licence: Paraphrased for education. Copyright World Health Organization; see who.int terms of use.

title: Daily fibre
text: Anyone older than 10 should aim for at least 25 g of fibre a day.
licence: Paraphrased for education. Copyright World Health Organization; see who.int terms of use.

title: Carbohydrate quality
text: Carbohydrate usually makes up about 45% to 75% of daily energy, and most of it should come from unrefined sources. Whole grains, vegetables, fruit and pulses such as lentils and beans are good examples.
licence: Paraphrased for education. Copyright World Health Organization; see who.int terms of use.

title: Everyday protein
text: Protein usually makes up about 10% to 15% of daily energy. That is roughly 50 g to 75 g a day on a 2,000 kcal diet.
licence: Paraphrased for education. Copyright World Health Organization; see who.int terms of use.

title: Daily potassium
text: The daily potassium goal is about 90 mmol, which is 3,510 mg.
licence: Paraphrased for education. Copyright World Health Organization; see who.int terms of use.

title: Salt and sodium limit
text: Keep sodium below 2,000 mg a day, which is less than 5 g of salt. 1 g of salt contains 400 mg of sodium.
licence: Paraphrased for education. Copyright World Health Organization; see who.int terms of use.

title: Where salt comes from
text: Common sources of sodium include processed food, bread, processed meat, salty snacks, soy sauce and fish sauce.
licence: Paraphrased for education. Copyright World Health Organization; see who.int terms of use.

title: Cutting down on salt
text: Choose fresh food more often and take the salt shaker off the table. Cook with only a little salt, flavour food with herbs and spices, and limit sauces and instant products.
licence: Paraphrased for education. Copyright World Health Organization; see who.int terms of use.

title: A balanced plate
text: Fruit and vegetables should make up just over a third of what you eat. Starchy foods should make up just over another third, with wholegrain versions where possible.
licence: Paraphrased for education. Crown copyright; see nhs.uk terms.

title: Five a day and juice
text: Aim for at least 5 portions of fruit and vegetables a day. Keep fruit juice to 150 ml a day.
licence: Paraphrased for education. Crown copyright; see nhs.uk terms.

title: Fish and red meat
text: Eat at least 2 portions of fish a week, including 1 portion of oily fish. Eat less red and processed meat.
licence: Paraphrased for education. Crown copyright; see nhs.uk terms.

title: How much to drink
text: Aim for 6 to 8 drinks a day.
licence: Paraphrased for education. Crown copyright; see nhs.uk terms.

title: Average daily energy
text: On average, women need about 2,000 kcal a day and men about 2,500 kcal a day.
licence: Paraphrased for education. Crown copyright; see nhs.uk terms.

title: Weekly activity for adults
text: Adults should do at least 150 minutes of moderate activity a week. Any amount is better than none. Limit the time you spend sitting, and know that strength work benefits everyone.
licence: Paraphrased for education. Copyright World Health Organization; see who.int terms of use.

title: What counts as activity
text: Physical activity covers many forms of movement. Walking, wheeling and cycling all count, so activity does not have to be a gym workout.
licence: Paraphrased for education. Copyright World Health Organization; see who.int terms of use.

title: Moderate or vigorous minutes
text: Adults can do 150 minutes of moderate activity or 75 minutes of vigorous activity a week. Some activity is still better than none.
source: CDC, Physical activity guidelines for adults
licence: Paraphrased for education. See cdc.gov website policies.

title: Strength training days
text: Adults should strengthen their muscles on at least 2 days a week, working all the major muscle groups.
source: CDC, Physical activity guidelines for adults
licence: Paraphrased for education. See cdc.gov website policies.

title: Spreading activity over the week
text: Spread your activity over 4 to 5 days a week. Break up long periods of sitting.
source: NHS, Physical activity guidelines for adults aged 19 to 64
licence: Paraphrased for education. Crown copyright; see nhs.uk terms.

title: The talk test for intensity
text: During moderate activity you can still talk but you cannot sing. During vigorous activity you can only say a few words before pausing for breath.
source: NHS, Physical activity guidelines for adults aged 19 to 64
licence: Paraphrased for education. Crown copyright; see nhs.uk terms.

title: Starting when inactive or unwell
text: If you have been inactive or have a health condition, see a GP before starting a new exercise routine.
source: NHS, Physical activity guidelines for adults aged 19 to 64
licence: Paraphrased for education. Crown copyright; see nhs.uk terms.

title: How much sleep
text: Adults aged 18 to 60 need at least 7 hours of sleep a night. Adults aged 61 to 64 need 7 to 9 hours, and people aged 65 or older need 7 to 8 hours. Teenagers need 8 to 10 hours.
licence: Paraphrased for education. See cdc.gov website policies.

title: Bedroom and bedtime habits
text: Go to bed and get up at the same times each day. Keep the bedroom quiet and cool. Turn off electronic devices 30 minutes before bed.
licence: Paraphrased for education. See cdc.gov website policies.

title: Food and drink before bed
text: Avoid large meals and alcohol before bed. Avoid caffeine in the afternoon.
licence: Paraphrased for education. See cdc.gov website policies.

title: When sleep problems continue
text: If sleep problems continue, talk to a health care provider.
licence: Paraphrased for education. See cdc.gov website policies.

title: Lowering the risk of type 2 diabetes
text: Keeping a healthy weight and being active for at least 150 minutes a week help prevent type 2 diabetes. Eat a healthy diet that avoids sugar and saturated fat, and do not use tobacco.
licence: Paraphrased for education. Copyright World Health Organization; see who.int terms of use.

title: Regular checks with diabetes
text: People with diabetes need regular checks of their feet, kidneys and eyes.
licence: Paraphrased for education. Copyright World Health Organization; see who.int terms of use.

title: The plate method for diabetes
text: Fill half the plate with nonstarchy vegetables, a quarter with high-fibre carbohydrates and a quarter with protein. Choose drinks with little or no added sugar.
licence: Paraphrased for education. See niddk.nih.gov website policies.

title: Activity with diabetes
text: Adults with diabetes should aim for 150 minutes of activity a week, strength work 2 days a week and balance work 2 to 3 days a week. Check blood glucose before, during and after activity.
licence: Paraphrased for education. See niddk.nih.gov website policies.

title: Alcohol with diabetes
text: For people who use insulin, alcohol can cause low blood glucose.
licence: Paraphrased for education. See niddk.nih.gov website policies.

title: Sleep with diabetes
text: People with diabetes should aim for 7 to 8 hours of sleep.
licence: Paraphrased for education. See niddk.nih.gov website policies.

title: Exercise and low blood glucose
text: For many people, low blood glucose means below 70 mg/dL. Exercise can keep lowering blood glucose for up to 24 hours. Check your level and carry fast-acting carbohydrate with you.
licence: Paraphrased for education. See niddk.nih.gov website policies.

title: Treating low blood glucose
text: The usual first step for low blood glucose is 15 to 20 g of carbohydrate, then check again after 15 minutes. Severe low blood glucose needs glucagon and emergency help. Follow the plan agreed with your care team.
licence: Paraphrased for education. See niddk.nih.gov website policies.

title: What counts as high blood pressure
text: High blood pressure is diagnosed when readings are 140/90 or higher on 2 different days.
licence: Paraphrased for education. Copyright World Health Organization; see who.int terms of use.

title: Living with high blood pressure
text: Eat a low-salt diet and do 150 minutes of moderate or 75 minutes of vigorous activity a week. Add strength work on at least 2 days, sit less and limit alcohol. Take medicine as prescribed.
licence: Paraphrased for education. Copyright World Health Organization; see who.int terms of use.
